newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1996 economic situation best since 1993.
newsitem.headline: China 1996 economic situation best since 1993.

text.p: China's economic development has maintained steady growth in the first eight months of this year with the economy giving its best performance since 1993, Xinhua news agency quoted on Monday Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji as saying.

All macro-economic indicators had basically met state targets set at the start of the year, Zhu told a three-day conference on cotton that closed last Thursday. "Some are even better than expected," he was quoted as saying.
China had enhanced macro-economic control without sacrificing its rapid and sustained economic growth and without causing any obvious rise in unemployment in urban areas, Zhu said.
Since the beginning of the year, consumer demand had grown steadily, investment in fixed assets had risen sensibly and foreign trade has increased steadily, he said.
The rise in overall national economic demand had exceeded the speed of economic growth, and no problem of stagnant demand existed, he said.

Revenues had increased rapidly while price rises had cooled and bank deposits had risen despite two cuts in interest rates, in May and in August, and the scrapping of the interest rate subsidy, he said.

While harvests in some areas had been hit by floods in recent months, the summer harvest along with early rice were expected to rise with the good agricultural situation providing a sound foundation for a strong economy, he said.

The current fall in profits of state-owned enterprises and increase in losses were not attributable to falling demand but to an outdated management system that did not fit requirements of a market economy and to output of products with no market.

These problems had accumulated over many years and could not be solved by large investments or a relaxation of bank credits, he said, apparently responding to widespread recent pleas from state firm managers for more bank loans.

State firms' losses since last year did not reflect the economic situation, he said. He said rises in prices of grain and cotton had cut into state firms's profits by raising costs but a good harvest would ease this problem.

Reforms to the financial management of state firms had reduced the rate of depreciation, shifting profits of some enterprises into capital and strengthening their ability to improve, he said. In addition, changes to the social welfare system that had cut their burden of pensions and unemployment care had boosted some firms, he said.
However, some local governments were randomly collecting fees from enterprises while many suffered from poor management while others had raised wages excessively, he said.
The two interest rates cuts had reduced interest repayment for state firms by 70 billion yuan this year, he said.

An acceleration in repayment of export tax rebates, to 12 billion yuan in January-August had further helped, he said, adding that their economic returns have begun to improve in the past two months and exports had increased.
On cotton, he said the State Council, or cabinet, had decided not to throw open the cotton market, raw material prices or administration over cotton growing this year.

Zhu said new problems involving cotton output, circulation and consumer demand reflected longstanding problems in the textile industry such as low levels of production, surplus production capacity, poor quality and outdated products.

This year, regions will form cotton trading associations that will replace the state allocation system, he said. Chinese officials have forecast this year's harvest at 3.8 million tonnes, down from 4.5 million last year, and compared with demand for 5.0 million tonnes.
He urged finance, tax authorities and marketing cooperatives to seek ways to help textile mills overcome their problems to reactivate the industry.
